hosted.body: We host your website and dashboard. Use an included address or connect your own domain when you’re ready.

wordpress.title: Keep your WordPress site
wordpress.body: Add BranchHarbor forms, schedules and connections to the site you already have. Your hosting stays the same.

integrations.title: Works with what you use

evidence.title: Pilot results will be published here
evidence.body: We don’t show customer logos or performance claims before we have them. Until pilot businesses report back, explore the workflows themselves.

pricing.title: Billed per location
pricing.body: Pay for the locations you authorise, in your currency. Keep your existing booking or commerce software where we connect to it. Networks get onboarding help.

items.a: You pay for each location you authorise in BranchHarbor. Adding a location doesn’t publish its website automatically, and removing one stops billing from the next period.

items.q: Do I have to replace my existing software?
items.a: No. Where we support a connection, your booking or commerce system stays authoritative and BranchHarbor works alongside it. Every module says whether it replaces, embeds or only reports on a workflow.

items.q: How much control do locations keep?
items.a: Headquarters decides which fields are locked, editable or need approval. Locations see that origin on every field and can request changes.
A setup checklist that saves as you go, help importing locations, and for networks a guided rollout with your team.

items.q: Does it work in my country and language?
items.a: BranchHarbor is built for businesses in North America, the UK and Europe, Australia and New Zealand, Asia, the Middle East and Latin America. Each location keeps its own time zone and currency, and the interface is available in several languages. Payment availability depends on your provider and country.

studios.imageAlt: Group yoga class in a studio
studios.headline: Keep every studio connected, from first enquiry to the next class.
studios.intro: Websites, schedules, enquiries and instructor cover in one place, with each studio keeping its own calendar and members.

problems.t: One site per studio, all slightly different
problems.d: Schedules, prices and intro offers drift between locations and nobody is sure which page is current.
Trial requests sit unanswered because they went to a shared address nobody owns.
Instructor swaps happen in messages and the public schedule shows the wrong name.

workflow.label: Enquiry
workflow.title: An enquiry reaches the right studio
workflow.desc: Website forms route to the studio the visitor chose. Managers see new enquiries with their source and can reply or book a trial.

workflow.label: Trial
workflow.title: Trial booked with an eligible offer
workflow.desc: The intro offer applies only to new members at that studio. The booking system remains authoritative where it is connected.

workflow.label: Class
workflow.title: Classes, capacity and waitlists
workflow.desc: Week and day views per studio. Edit one occurrence or a whole series, with a preview of who is affected.

workflow.label: Membership
workflow.title: Members, packs and attendance
workflow.desc: Searchable member records with pack balance, membership state and consent. Other studios can’t see these details unless policy allows.

hq: Shared class types, descriptions and brand pages
Intro offers that studios can opt into
Network reports on enquiries and attendance where connected
local: Local prices where HQ allows overrides

faqs.q: Do we have to replace our booking software?
faqs.a: No. In the first release, a supported booking system stays authoritative and BranchHarbor shows its schedule and links to it. Native booking comes later and only replaces your system if you choose it.

faqs.q: Can headquarters see member details at every studio?
faqs.a: Not automatically. Network reports show totals. Member records stay with the studio unless your business policy allows sharing for a stated purpose.

faqs.q: What happens with daylight-saving changes?
faqs.a: Classes are stored in UTC and shown in each studio’s local time zone, so recurring times stay correct across the change, wherever the studio is.

sports.imageAlt: Children playing football on a grass field
sports.headline: Bring programmes, teams and venues into one organised home.
sports.intro: Registrations, rosters, schedules and attendance for every venue, with guardians seeing only the participants they represent.

problems.d: Paper, spreadsheets and form tools that don’t talk to the roster.

problems.t: Venue clashes found on the day
problems.d: Two groups booked on the same pitch because schedules live in different places.
Parents get updates for the wrong group, or none at all.

workflow.label: Register
workflow.title: Guardians register a participant
workflow.desc: Choose programme and venue, confirm eligibility by age-boundary date, link the participant to the guardian and complete required forms.

workflow.label: Assign
workflow.title: Review and assign groups
workflow.desc: Payment never equals selection. Administrators review registrations and assign groups and coaches.

workflow.label: Schedule
workflow.title: Schedules with venue conflicts flagged
workflow.desc: Training and fixtures by venue, with clashes highlighted before they reach families.

workflow.label: Attendance
workflow.title: Fast check-in for coaches
workflow.desc: Coaches open their session, see the authorised roster and record attendance in a few taps.

hq: Programme templates, fees and registration forms
local: Session updates to affected groups only

faqs.q: Does paying mean a child is on the team?
faqs.a: No. Where approval is required, the confirmation says the registration is pending review. Payment and selection are separate steps.

faqs.q: Can a coach see every participant?
faqs.a: Coaches see only the rosters for sessions they are assigned to.

faqs.q: Will AI choose players?
faqs.a: No. AI can draft programme descriptions and summarise enrolment. It never selects children based on inferred ability or sensitive characteristics.

wellness.imageAlt: Client relaxing during a spa treatment
wellness.headline: Make service booking simpler for clients and local teams.
wellness.intro: Services, practitioners, rooms and repeat appointments, with buffers enforced and the original slot kept safe during rescheduling.

problems.d: Two calendars promise the same treatment room.
Clients cancel to rebook and the original time is gone if the new one fails.
Administrative notes are visible to staff who don’t need them.

workflow.label: Service
workflow.title: Clients choose a service
workflow.desc: Each service sets duration, price, buffers, eligible practitioners and the resources it needs.

workflow.label: Practitioner
workflow.title: Practitioner or any available
workflow.desc: Availability respects location assignments, service eligibility and room capacity together.

workflow.label: Appointment
workflow.title: Practitioner and room secured together
workflow.desc: A reservation holds both the practitioner and the room. Deposits and cancellation terms are shown before payment.

workflow.label: Repeat
workflow.title: Packages and safe rescheduling
workflow.desc: The old slot is released only after the new one is secured. If the change fails, the original appointment stays.

faqs.q: Is this a clinical records system?
faqs.a: No. The first release is administrative. Diagnosis, clinical records and treatment recommendations are out of scope.

faqs.q: Does AI read intake forms?
faqs.a: Sensitive form responses are excluded from general AI context by default.

faqs.q: What if a reschedule fails?
faqs.a: Your existing appointment stays in place. Nothing is released until the replacement is confirmed.

commerce.headline: Coordinate your catalogue. Let every store serve its customers.
commerce.intro: A shared catalogue with local stock and pricing, a WooCommerce connection, and an inventory history instead of a single number.

problems.d: The site says in stock; the shelf says otherwise.
A store edit silently changes product content for everyone.
A failed sync creates the same order twice.

workflow.label: Catalogue
workflow.title: Master products with editable fields
workflow.desc: HQ creates products and variants, sets which fields stores can edit, and previews before distribution.

workflow.label: Assortment
workflow.title: Local stock and permitted prices
workflow.desc: Stores adjust availability and stock with a reason. Override origin is always visible.

workflow.label: Order
workflow.title: Orders with clear payment and fulfilment
workflow.desc: Every order shows its source system, payment state and fulfilment state separately.

workflow.label: Returns
workflow.title: Returns, reviewed and resolved
workflow.desc: Requested, reviewed, authorised, received and resolved, with refunds recorded against the original payment.

faqs.q: Does BranchHarbor replace WooCommerce checkout?
faqs.a: No. Your existing gateways and checkout stay. We never insert a second checkout automatically.

faqs.q: What if a store edits a product?
faqs.a: Only fields HQ marked editable can change, and the change is stored as a local override that never touches master content.

faqs.q: How are stores in different currencies reported?
faqs.a: Amounts always keep their currency. Network reports total each currency separately rather than converting them with an undisclosed rate.

foods.imageAlt: Chef preparing vegetables in a restaurant kitchen
foods.headline: One brand menu. Local control. Clear ordering.
foods.intro: Master menus with local overrides, pickup ordering with real slot capacity, and a kitchen view built for a busy line.

problems.d: A price change reaches some locations and not others.

problems.t: Pickup times that can’t be met
problems.d: Online orders ignore how busy the kitchen already is.

problems.t: Orders lost on a bad connection
problems.d: The tablet shows stale orders as if they were current.

workflow.label: Menu
workflow.title: Brand menu, published to locations
workflow.desc: HQ manages items, modifiers and business-supplied dietary details, then publishes with per-location results.

workflow.label: Pickup
workflow.title: Pickup slots with real capacity
workflow.desc: Customers choose a pickup time first. Slots, cutoffs and preparation buffers are checked on the server before confirmation.

workflow.label: Order
workflow.title: Awaiting acceptance vs accepted
workflow.desc: Customers see clearly whether the restaurant has accepted their order. Rejection triggers a void or refund and a notice.

workflow.label: Kitchen
workflow.title: A kitchen view for a busy line
workflow.desc: Large cards sorted by promised time, overdue markers, optional alerts and a clear warning when the connection drops.

hq: Menu items, modifiers and dietary details

faqs.q: Can AI write allergen information?
faqs.a: No. Allergen and dietary information comes from your business. AI can draft menu copy but can’t change ingredients, dietary labels, prices or order acceptance.

faqs.q: What happens if the kitchen tablet loses connection?
faqs.a: The screen shows the last refresh time and pauses status changes so stale orders aren’t presented as current.

faqs.q: What if a payment arrives but the order doesn’t?
faqs.a: Payment and order mismatches appear in a recovery queue for staff to resolve.

realty.imageAlt: Modern detached house with large windows
realty.headline: Every office, every listing, one trusted network.
realty.intro: Listings with HQ advertising checks, enquiries routed to the right agent, viewings booked from real availability and offers with a full trail — across countries and currencies.

problems.d: Offices publish copy and disclosures that HQ never reviewed.
Portal and website enquiries land in shared inboxes with no owner.
Network volume adds dollars, pounds and euros as if they were one.

workflow.label: Listings
workflow.title: From draft to sold, with HQ checks
workflow.desc: Managed and standard offices publish after HQ approval; changes to live listings wait for approval too. Disclosures come from the business.

workflow.label: Enquiries
workflow.title: Every lead has an owner
workflow.desc: Website and portal enquiries go to the listing agent, then round-robin, then the office pool. Agents see their own leads and the pool.

workflow.label: Viewings
workflow.title: Viewings from real availability
workflow.desc: Buyers book free slots from the agents' calendars in the office time zone. An agent can never be double-booked.

workflow.label: Offers
workflow.title: Offers with a full trail
workflow.desc: Counter, accept or reject with every step recorded. Only the listing agents, the buyer's agent and office managers see offers.

hq: Office governance tiers and advertising checks
Network reports per currency, without client details

faqs.q: Can AI write listing descriptions?
faqs.a: AI drafts descriptions from the facts you enter and never adds features, views or neighbourhood claims. It refuses requests that target or exclude people by protected characteristics, and every draft needs your approval.

faqs.q: Do you send listings to property portals?
faqs.a: Not yet. Portal feed formats can be previewed in a sandbox, but no portal connection is live and nothing is sent.

faqs.q: Who can see offers?
faqs.a: The listing agents, the buyer's agent for their own offer, and office managers. Headquarters sees network totals without client details by default.

franchises.imageAlt: Instructor leading a class in a bright studio
franchises.headline: Coordinate the brand. Trust each location.
franchises.intro: Headquarters, regions, owner groups and locations, each with scoped roles. Shared templates go out with a review table; locations run their day.

points.d: Owner groups can operate several locations. Users can hold more than one assignment, across countries.
Every template field shows its origin, and local overrides can be reset to HQ defaults.
Network reports don’t grant access to customer details. Cross-location sharing needs an explicit policy.
Group publishing reports per location, with version snapshots and rollback.

steps.d: Import locations with row-level validation and assign owner groups.
Choose what is shared, what is local and what needs approval.
Regional managers, franchise owners and staff see only their assignments.
Review tables before every shared change and per-location results after.

franchises.intlTitle: Built for networks that cross borders

intl.d: Each location keeps its own time zone and currency. Reports total each currency separately.
Locations can publish in their own language while sharing brand templates.
Organisations choose a data region (US, EU or Asia-Pacific) when they are created.

independent.imageAlt: Owner opening the door of a small shop
independent.headline: Everything in one place, without network complexity.
independent.intro: One location and a small team, without network complexity: no scope selector, regions or approval chains. Open a second location later and upgrade to the network tools in a few clicks. Everything you have is kept.

points.d: Your business name replaces the location picker. Overview, reports and AI answers are about your business, not a network.
Business details, address, hours, time zone and currency in a single step. Progress saves as you go, and optional steps can wait.
No locked fields or approval chains. Edit your website and publish; turn on approvals only if you want to check staff changes first.

points.t: Simple roles for a small team
points.d: Invite a manager, staff, a marketing contributor or a finance user. Network roles stay out of the way.

steps.d: Verify your email, then choose your industry and “independent business”.
Name, address, time zone, currency and opening hours in one step.

steps.t: Add your classes, services, products or menu

independent.signupNote: Self-service sign-up is open for studios. Other industries start with a short demo while they are in pilot.
independent.upgradeBody: Add a location from Settings. BranchHarbor explains what changes, you confirm, and your business becomes a network. Only the owner can do it, and the change is logged.

upgradePoints.d: Your location, customers, website, team and payment history stay as they are.
Locations directory, scope selector, regions, owner groups, templates and group publishing.
Your website gains a location finder and each location gets its own page.

steps.d: We list relevant plugins we found and tell you what we checked.

Least-privilege access with an application password, never your login.

Import, export or both, with conflict rules.

statusHelp.tested: Tested against the named versions, with documented actions and limits.
statusHelp.limited: Works for the listed actions only. Check the limits before relying on it.

integrations.disclaimer: Statuses describe the current pre-release build and are reviewed before launch. Product names belong to their owners; listing does not imply partnership or endorsement.

woocommerce.desc: Products, stock and orders through supported APIs, with HPOS handling and declared checkout compatibility.
woocommerce.truth: WooCommerce owns orders and checkout. BranchHarbor owns the master catalogue when you choose it.
woocommerce.limit: Custom checkout fields need mapping. Subscriptions extension not supported yet.

gutenberg.desc: BranchHarbor schedules, forms and menus as native blocks.
gutenberg.limit: Full-site editing templates tested on default themes only.

yoast.desc: Coexists without writing metadata. BranchHarbor blocks defer to Yoast for titles and sitemaps.
yoast.truth: Yoast owns metadata, canonical URLs and sitemaps.

wprocket.desc: Coexists with documented exclusions for dynamic and authenticated paths.
wprocket.limit: Add the listed exclusions after install.

stripe.desc: Connected accounts per business or location for payments in supported countries. Eligibility and fees are set by Stripe.
stripe.truth: Stripe owns payment state. BranchHarbor records references and reconciles.
stripe.limit: Independently owned franchises may need separate accounts. Availability varies by country.

mailchimp.desc: Export consented contacts by location to audiences.
mailchimp.truth: BranchHarbor owns consent; Mailchimp owns sends.
mailchimp.limit: Only contacts with recorded consent export.

twilio.desc: SMS reminders and notifications sent through your Twilio account.
twilio.limit: You supply the account and sender numbers; country sender rules apply.

gravityforms.desc: Map form fields to BranchHarbor leads and route by location.
gravityforms.truth: Gravity Forms owns the submission; BranchHarbor stores the lead.

multisite.desc: Network authorisation plus an explicit connection per site and location.
multisite.truth: Each site keeps its own content.

ga4.desc: Add your Google Analytics 4 measurement ID to hosted sites, with consent handling.
ga4.limit: No data is imported back into BranchHarbor reports.

googlecalendar.limit: One-way only; edits in Google are not imported.

elementor.desc: Shortcode and embed widgets inside Elementor layouts.
elementor.limit: No native widget yet; styling inherits from the theme.

wpml.desc: Language mapping for translated pages and records.

mindbody.desc: Class schedules and bookings from Mindbody.
mindbody.limit: Not available. API access under review.

momence.desc: Class schedules and memberships from Momence.

janeapp.desc: Appointments and practitioner availability from Jane.

teamsnap.desc: Rosters and schedules for clubs already using TeamSnap.

adyen.desc: Payments for larger networks that already use Adyen.

paypal.desc: PayPal as an additional payment method on hosted checkouts.

square.desc: In-store sales and catalogue for retail and food.

lightspeed.desc: Retail and hospitality POS sales and stock.

shopify.desc: Products and orders for stores already selling on Shopify.

googlebusiness.desc: Keep hours and location details in sync with Google Business Profile.

meta.desc: Lead forms from Facebook and Instagram routed to the right location.

whatsapp.desc: Order and appointment updates through WhatsApp Business.

features: Bookings, orders and payments for your industry
Simple roles for a small team
Upgrade to Network when you open a second location

hosted.name: Hosted
features: Included address or your own domain

pricing.ctaNote: During the pilot, connector and network plans start with a conversation so we can confirm your industry and connections are supported. Solo sign-up is self-service for studios.

faqs.q: Why do prices differ between currencies?
faqs.a: Each currency has its own list price, set for that market. We don’t convert with a live exchange rate, so the price you see is the price you pay (plus any applicable tax).

faqs.q: Is tax included?
faqs.a: No. VAT, GST, sales tax or similar may apply depending on your country and business details. Applicable tax is shown before you confirm.

faqs.q: Can different locations pay in different currencies?
faqs.a: Networks can be billed per location or centrally. Each invoice uses one currency; we never add amounts in different currencies together.

faqs.q: Are payment-processing fees included?
faqs.a: No. Payments go through a connected provider such as Stripe, which charges its own fees in your country.

faqs.q: What happens if I open a second location?
faqs.a: Solo covers one location. When you add another, you upgrade to Network from Settings: your website, customers, team and history are kept, and billing moves to per-location pricing once the new location is operating.

pricing.soloTotal: One location. Add more by moving to Network.

about.headline: Individual branches, one shared home.
about.intro: BranchHarbor helps independent businesses, multi-location operators and franchise networks manage their websites, local customer activity and industry workflows in one coordinated place — wherever their locations are.
about.purpose: Multi-location businesses run on disconnected websites, inconsistent local content, campaigns that are hard to report on and integrations nobody fully trusts. Headquarters needs oversight; local teams need room to run their day. We think both can be true at once.

principles.d: Plain language for owners, consequences explained before broad changes.
Each branch keeps its identity while drawing on a shared home.
Planned features are labelled. No invented customers or claims.
We release one complete vertical at a time, measured with real businesses.

privacy.title: Privacy notice
privacy.intro: This notice explains how BranchHarbor handles personal data when you visit our website, request a demo or use the BranchHarbor service, and how we process customer data on behalf of the businesses that use us.

sections.h: Who we are and our role
p: For our website, demo requests and account administration, BranchHarbor is the controller (or “business” under US state privacy laws) of your personal data.

For customer data that businesses store in BranchHarbor — such as members, clients, participants or guests — the business is the controller and BranchHarbor acts as a processor (or “service provider”) following their instructions.
Demo requests: name, work email, business name, industry, location count, country and any details you choose to share, used to respond to your request. Marketing emails are sent only if you opt in.
Website usage: basic technical data such as pages visited and browser type, used to operate and secure the site. Non-essential analytics run only with consent where the law requires it.

Under the GDPR and UK GDPR we rely on legitimate interests to respond to enquiries and secure our services, contract to provide the service, consent for marketing and non-essential cookies, and legal obligation where applicable.
We use service providers for hosting, email and support under written agreements. We do not sell personal data or share it for cross-context behavioural advertising.

Organisations choose a data region (US, EU or Asia-Pacific). Where data is transferred internationally we use appropriate safeguards such as Standard Contractual Clauses or the UK International Data Transfer Addendum.

We keep demo-request data for as long as needed to respond and follow up, then delete or anonymise it. Customer data is kept according to the business’s settings and deleted after account closure following a stated period.

Depending on where you live you may have rights to access, correct, delete or port your data, to object to or restrict processing, and to withdraw consent — including under the GDPR, UK GDPR, Canada’s PIPEDA, California’s CCPA/CPRA, Australia’s Privacy Act and Brazil’s LGPD.
If your data is held by a business that uses BranchHarbor, contact that business first; we will assist them. You can also complain to your local data-protection authority.
Contact details for privacy requests and, where required, our EU and UK representatives will be published here before launch.

terms.title: Terms of service
terms.intro: These draft terms outline the agreement between BranchHarbor and the businesses that use it. Final terms, including governing law and the contracting entity for each region, will be published before launch.

p: The business that creates an organisation is responsible for the users it invites and the roles it assigns, including at franchise and location level.
Plans are billed per authorised location in the currency shown at purchase. Taxes such as VAT, GST or sales tax are added where applicable. Removing a location stops billing from the next period.
Connected systems (for example payment providers or booking software) are governed by their own terms. Each integration states which system is authoritative and what data is exchanged.
You keep ownership of your content and your customers’ data. We process it only to provide the service and as described in our data processing terms.
Don’t use BranchHarbor to send unsolicited messages, infringe rights, misrepresent your business or break local laws, including consumer-protection and marketing-consent rules in your country.
Liability limits will be set out in the final terms. Nothing in these terms limits rights that cannot be limited under your local law, including statutory consumer rights.
We will give notice of material changes before they take effect.

security.title: Security practices
security.intro: How we intend to protect the businesses that use BranchHarbor and their customers. This describes design commitments for the pre-release service, not independent certifications.

p: Every request is scoped to one organisation. Roles are assigned at organisation, region, owner-group or location level, and network reports never grant access to customer records by themselves.
Staff access to a customer account must be authorised, time-limited and logged in the audit trail visible to the business.
Card details are handled by connected payment providers. BranchHarbor stores tokens and references, never raw card numbers.
Connections use scoped credentials such as OAuth tokens or WordPress application passwords — never your primary password. Credentials are encrypted at rest and can be revoked at any time.
Organisations choose a data region (US, EU or Asia-Pacific). Data is encrypted in transit and at rest.
We will notify affected businesses without undue delay and support them in meeting their own notification duties under laws such as the GDPR, UK GDPR and PIPEDA.
A responsible-disclosure contact and policy will be published here before launch. Please don’t test against accounts you don’t own.
